statement: For iid finite almost surely nonnegative nearest-neighbour edge weights on Z^2, n>=1 and r>0, E[T(0,n e1)^r]<infinity if and only if E[min(t1,t2,t3,t4)^r]<infinity. More precisely, with L=n+8 and K=n(n+2)^2(n+8), P(M>t)<=P(T>t)<=K P(M>t/L) for all t>=0.
assumptions: iid finite almost surely nonnegative edge weights
proof_or_counterexample: Four explicit edge-disjoint paths of lengths n,n+2,n+2,n+8; independence applies only to their disjoint edge sets. Lower bound is the minimum of the four edges incident to the origin. Integrate the resulting two tail bounds.
independent_reviewer: w367 KEEP with scope; final w368 referee verdict pending
remaining_gap: No mathematical gap asserted in this fixed-endpoint moment criterion; constants depend on n. No fixed-law KPZ power estimate follows.

statement: For iid continuous Pareto weights supported on [1,infinity) with tail index alpha>0 on the square lattice, E[T(0,n e1)^r]<infinity iff 4 alpha>r, for n>=1 and r>0. At alpha=1/2 the mean is finite and Var(T)=infinity.
assumptions: same lattice and iid hypotheses as C1
proof_or_counterexample: Integrate t^(r-1-4 alpha) and apply C1; both equality endpoints diverge.
independent_reviewer: w367 KEEP with scope; final w368 referee verdict pending
remaining_gap: Only counters an extension lacking moment hypotheses; does not refute the standard KPZ target.

statement: If all square-lattice edge weights lie in [1,1+epsilon], then T(0,n e1) is exactly the straight-path sum for n epsilon<=2. For iid Uniform[1,1+epsilon], Var(T)=n epsilon^2/12 in that window; for n epsilon>2 the straight path loses to a dogleg with positive probability.
assumptions: deterministic support for the identity; iid Uniform for variance and probabilistic sharpness
proof_or_counterexample: Parity forces every nonstraight route to have at least n+2 edges. Compare n(1+epsilon) to n+2. Beyond the boundary prescribe high straight weights and low weights on an edge-disjoint dogleg.
independent_reviewer: w367 KEEP with scope; final w368 referee verdict pending
remaining_gap: The finite window depends on epsilon; nothing here yields a fixed-law asymptotic exponent.

statement: For every beta<1, no finite C independent of the edge law and n can satisfy Var_F(T(0,n e1))<=C Var_F(t_e) n^beta for all iid Uniform[1,1+epsilon] laws, epsilon>0, n>=1. A common law-independent starting scale does not repair this.
assumptions: C and any starting scale independent of epsilon
proof_or_counterexample: Set epsilon=1/n; C3 makes the variance ratio exactly n^(1-beta), which is unbounded.

statement: For iid edge weights in [1,1+epsilon] with variance sigma^2 and n epsilon<2, the geodesic from 0 to n e1 is the deterministic straight path before and after independent edge refresh with probability delta. Overlap equals n, Cov(T,T^delta)=(1-delta)n sigma^2, and E[(T-T^delta)^2]=2 delta n sigma^2.
assumptions: independent edge refresh probability delta in [0,1]
proof_or_counterexample: Strict support comparison gives the unique straight route in both environments. Compute the covariance of each refreshed edge pair and sum independent deterministic edges.
remaining_gap: No law-dependent asymptotic chaos estimate follows; this only refutes a law-uniform overlap bridge.
